source.binding_note: candidate_head names the parent of the commit carrying this artifact. Enforced by scripts/check_capability_evidence_binding.mjs, which lands on the gateway-boundaries lane.

change_scope: Edge Function parity evidence and a capability-preserving rollback procedure. Documentation and evidence only; no runtime, application, database, or provider state is modified.

review_remediation.finding: the rollback document named d0e689556cc01428500b796cade87032ea5c0ad8 as the full-capability target, but canonical main has advanced to aa228d5bfb59c0e54ed85415d6faaea3340f6c56
review_remediation.consequence: rolling to the documented SHA would silently discard everything merged after it, so it no longer proves capability-preserving rollback
review_remediation.fix: artifact identifiers are validated against a per-provider allowlist of immutable id shapes; a provider with no registered shape cannot contribute a target at all
review_remediation.recurrence_prevention: the rollback target is selected from docs/rollback/RELEASE_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY.json as an immutable provider artifact. scripts/check_rollback_targets.mjs enforces the registry contract and cross-checks that this artifact's release_candidate_artifact_id names a QUALIFIED registry entry, so durable evidence and validator cannot drift apart.
review_remediation.parity_manifest_updated: canonical_commit refreshed to current main with a note to recompute if main advances
review_remediation.second_review_finding: replacing the stale fixed SHA with "whatever origin/main points at" was itself unsafe: current main can contain work merged but never production-authorized, deployed, rehearsed, or verified, so promoting it mid-incident would ship unreleased changes rather than restore known-good state.
review_remediation.disqualified_target: dpl_9EkwxicRPzigkvUis5m1qk644CrG, which predates the ProjectOS health and Memory search routes
review_remediation.guard: scripts/check_rollback_targets.mjs, 32 self-tests, wired into npm run verify
unclosed_limitations: the qualified artifact capability manifest was not re-probed (Vercel unauthenticated in this session)
its source commit is asserted by prior evidence and was not independently rebound to the artifact
review_remediation.third_review_finding: the validator kept moving refs out with a blocklist of origin/*, refs/*, main and HEAD, so v1.2.3, release/foo and feature/x could be listed as artifacts, marked production_verified and qualify — reintroducing the moving-ref model the registry prohibits
review_remediation.cross_check: scripts/check_rollback_targets.mjs validates this artifact against the registry: release_candidate_artifact_id must name a QUALIFIED registry entry, the superseded prose field is rejected outright, and the resolution path independently re-asserts every target property rather than trusting the registry's own qualified flag.

superseded_statements.previously_asserted: the procedure instructs the operator to resolve the rollback target from origin/main
superseded_statements.status: REJECTED — a moving ref is not a valid rollback target

superseded_statements.previously_asserted: current canonical main, resolved at rollback time
superseded_statements.status: REJECTED — replaced by rollback.release_candidate_artifact_id naming an immutable provider artifact

review_remediation.fourth_review_finding: the durable evidence still asserted the origin/main model that the validator had already rejected, so code and evidence disagreed and a future operator reading the artifact could have been misled
review_remediation.fourth_review_fix: the rollback block now names an artifact id rather than prose, every rejected model is recorded with the review that rejected it, and a registry cross-check makes the disagreement mechanically impossible
review_remediation.fifth_review_finding: registry resolution required only that the named id EXIST and that the registry entry assert qualified=true. The properties behind that flag (production/rehearsal verification, capability completeness, exact source binding) were asserted only in validateRegistry(), a separate function. Called on its own, validateEvidenceAgainstRegistry() accepted an artifact that was unverified, capability-incomplete and had no source commit, purely because it claimed qualified=true.
review_remediation.fifth_review_fix: targetQualificationErrors() now holds the target properties in one place and is called from BOTH validateRegistry() and the resolution path, so resolution never depends on a self-asserted flag or on another checker having run first. A rollback target must additionally state how its source_commit was bound, so an asserted binding can never be mistaken for a verified one.
review_remediation.fifth_review_defect_class: the same class as the rejected self-declared source.branch and the shape-only candidate_tree check: reading a flag the checked object controls, instead of asserting the underlying fact.
fifth_review_negative_tests: resolution alone: named artifact is unverified
resolution alone: named artifact drops capabilities
resolution alone: named artifact has no exact source
resolution alone: named artifact has unstated source binding
resolution alone: named artifact has no limitations array
resolution alone: every target property fails at once
registry: qualified without stated source binding
review_remediation.fifth_review_reproduced_before_fixing: yes — the rigged artifact was accepted with zero errors before the change and is rejected with five named reasons after it.

The registry's qualified flag is checked as well, but is not sufficient on its own.
